extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO disciplinary/reciprocal proceedings; OED staff and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline (exclusion/suspension) by the USPTO when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state authority, including the predicate offenses and required notices/administrative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline authority (37 C.F.R. § 11.24 / 35 U.S.C. § 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline (including exclusion) upon a practitioner based on disciplinary action by a duly constituted state authority; this action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the statutory/regulatory basis for imposing exclusion from practice before the USPTO. Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicate misconduct for exclusion — disbarment grounds (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State — predicates exclusion from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO imposed exclusion because Respondent's reciprocal discipline was predicated on his disbarment by the Supreme Court of California. A state disbarment is sufficient to support exclusion under § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and timeframe (Notice and Order; 40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be sent to the respondent and provide an opportunity to file a response opposing identical reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and provided Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of identical discipline based on one or more of the reasons listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). The Notice may also be published (here: two consecutive weeks in the Official Gazette). Failure to respond can lead to a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and to imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available defenses under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more of the reasons specified in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order references § 11.24(d)(1) as furnishing the permissible grounds for opposing identical discipline, and notes that the respondent was provided an opportunity to invoke those reasons in a timely response (40 days). The Order determined no genuine issue of material fact in light of the respondent's failure to file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper withdrawal / constructive termination (California Rule 3-700(A)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful violation of Cal. Rule of Professional Conduct 3-700(A)(2) for improper withdrawal by constructively terminating employment — failing to take any action on a client's behalf after notifying the client a patent application had been filed, and failing to inform the client that the attorney was withdrawing from employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count I in the underlying California decision found that the attorney 'constructively terminated' the relationship by not taking action and not properly notifying the client of withdrawal; such conduct served as a basis for state discipline and thus for reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to render an accounting (California Rule 4-100(B)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful violation of Cal. Rule 4-100(B)(3) for failing to render an accounting to a client of advanced fees and advanced costs after termination of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count 2 found the attorney failed to provide an accounting for $3,325 (breakdown given) advanced by the client. Failure to account for client funds is a disciplinary offense that can predicate reciprocal USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to return client papers/property (California Rule 3-700(D)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful violation of Cal. Rule 3-700(D)(1) for failing to promptly release all papers and property to a client upon the client's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count 3 found the respondent did not promptly return the client's file after a March 25, 2015 request. Failure to return client files/property is actionable misconduct supporting state discipline and reciprocal USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate with disciplinary investigation (BPC § 6068(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful violation of California Business & Professions Code § 6068(i) for failing to provide substantive responses to state bar inquiries/letters/emails during a disciplinary investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count 4 found the respondent received and failed to respond substantively to April 7 and 28, 2015 letters and a June 16, 2015 email from the California State Bar. Noncooperation with disciplinary authorities is a ground for discipline that may be recognized by the USPTO in reciprocal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral turpitude / dishonesty (BPC § 6106) — false statement to client
rubrics_metrics.description: Willful violation of BPC § 6106 for moral turpitude, dishonesty, or corruption: making a written representation to a client that a patent application had been filed when the attorney knew or was grossly negligent in not knowing that the statement was false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count 5 found the attorney knowingly or with gross negligence misrepresented to his client that a patent application had been filed. Dishonesty or statements involving moral turpitude are severe grounds leading to disbarment and reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative notifications and publication duties (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.59, Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish notice of exclusion in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication of a 'Notice of Exclusion' in the Official Gazette (text provided) and notice to relevant agencies and courts under § 11.59 as part of the administrative implementation of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during suspension/exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (duties incumbent upon suspended or excluded practitioners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically requires compliance with § 11.58; while the Order does not detail those duties, it mandates the respondent's adherence to them as part of the disciplinary consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires administrative dissociation of the respondent's identity from USPTO customer accounts and PKI, effectively revoking access tied to those credentials as part of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is prohibited from applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number, and from having his name added to any USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express condition of exclusion: no Customer Number access or association until formal reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.
